executive_summary.headline: A free video editor with an MCP port leads the week: Concat added 2,616 stars
executive_summary.body: jub0t/Concat runs captions, voice cloning and cutout locally, has no watermark or account, and lets an agent cut video through a built-in MCP server.

executive_summary.headline: Agent memory goes vendor-neutral
executive_summary.body: akitaonrails/ai-memory added 3,254 stars by letting Claude Code hand a half-finished task to Codex with a typed handoff, and agent-beacon added 972 on the same idea.

executive_summary.headline: Science agents arrive with evaluations
executive_summary.body: ChemGraph merged a Deep Agent evaluation harness, idfkit-mcp exposes 37 EnergyPlus tools to an assistant, and a chemistry skill library cites a peer-reviewed paper.

executive_summary.headline: Key takeaway
executive_summary.body: Individual builders are wrapping local tools in MCP and skills so agents can run them: video, 3D scans, TVs, simulators. Pick one real task this week and hand it to an agent through one of these.

top_picks.title: jub0t/Concat
top_picks.summary: Concat is a free, open-source video editor for macOS, Windows, Linux and Android that runs captions, text-to-speech, voice cloning and background removal on-device, with no watermark or account. It added 2,616 stars this week, and a built-in MCP server lets agents cut video with it.
top_picks.results: 2,616 weekly stars (GitHub Trending weekly snapshot, Oct 25 evening PT); 11,546 total; v0.2.8 released Oct 20; at least 100 commits in the window, latest Oct 25; AGPL-3.0, individual maintainer.
key_takeaways: Captions use local Whisper and the cutout and voice models download once, then work offline.
An MCP server (concat --mcp) and a JSON-RPC API let an agent drive the editor.
Aimed at TikTok, Reels, Shorts, tutorials and podcast clips.
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: The clever part is a full editor that an agent can drive over MCP while every model runs on the laptop. Experiment: point Claude at Concat and ask it to turn one internal demo recording into a captioned 60-second cut with a cloned narrator voice, then time it against a manual edit.

top_picks.title: akitaonrails/ai-memory
top_picks.summary: ai-memory gives coding agents one shared long-term memory: quit Claude Code mid-task, open Codex in the same directory and the next agent picks up a typed handoff of what failed and what is open. It added 3,254 stars this week and shipped v3.2.5 on Oct 25.
top_picks.results: 3,254 weekly stars (GitHub Trending weekly snapshot, Oct 25 evening PT); 13,528 total; v3.2.5 on Oct 25; at least 500 commits in the window (API page cap), latest Oct 25; README lists 20+ supported harnesses.
key_takeaways: Handoffs are a typed protocol: each has an owner and is claimed exactly once.
Works across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and others.
Single Rust binary, MIT license, built by an individual developer.
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: The clever part is treating the agent hand-off as a protocol instead of a chat summary, so switching tools mid-task stops costing context. Experiment: run a real task in one agent, stop halfway, and finish it in a different agent with ai-memory installed; see how much re-explaining you skip.

top_picks.title: wesbos/3d-model-anything
top_picks.summary: Wes Bos published an iPhone app, a Three.js viewer and a scan-to-threejs agent skill that turn a room capture into an editable 3D scene with a coding agent. The repo was created Oct 21 and has 1,924 stars; the README calls it an iterative reconstruction workflow, not one-click scan-to-model.
top_picks.results: 1,924 stars in its first five days (created Oct 21); 5 commits through Oct 22; includes a detailed office demo and a live viewer.
key_takeaways: The app records evidence; the skill guides measurement, modeling and matched-camera visual comparison.
Output is an editable Three.js scene, with dollhouse, walking, overhead and wireframe views.
Current focus is rooms and interiors.
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: The clever part is the matched-camera comparison loop, where the agent checks its model against the original photos until they agree. Experiment: scan one lab bench or meeting room with a phone and let an agent rebuild it as a browsable 3D scene over a weekend.

top_picks.title: idfkit/idfkit-mcp
top_picks.summary: idfkit-mcp is an MCP server that lets an assistant build, edit and simulate EnergyPlus building energy models in plain language. It exposes 37 tools and 13 resources, supports EnergyPlus 8.9 through 26.2, and shipped v0.11.0 and v0.11.1 in the window.
top_picks.results: 37 tools and 13 MCP resources; 18 EnergyPlus versions with bundled schemas; v0.11.1 on Oct 19 fixes start-up on Python 3.11. Star count is small (10), so the signal is the capability, not momentum. Science bonus +0.5 included in score.
key_takeaways: Describe a building and the agent creates zones, surfaces, constructions, schedules and HVAC.
Load an existing IDF or epJSON, edit it, validate, run a simulation and read results in one conversation.
Schema and documentation search return direct links to the EnergyPlus reference.
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: The clever part is a validated schema layer between the language model and a physics simulator, so an agent edits real building models without breaking them. Experiment: hand a building scientist a sample IDF and ask them to run three setpoint variants by chatting, then compare to their usual workflow time.

top_picks.title: ethanplusai/harvey
top_picks.summary: Harvey is an autonomous sales agent for small businesses that finds prospects, reads their sites, writes cold emails and drafts replies, running on a Claude or Codex subscription instead of per-token API billing. It added 1,147 stars this week and shipped v0.3.0 on Oct 13.
top_picks.results: 1,147 weekly stars (GitHub Trending weekly snapshot, Oct 25 evening PT); 2,548 total; at least 236 commits in the window; README cost table lists $0 to find businesses on the default source and $0 to read their websites (three HTTP requests, no model call).
key_takeaways: Website reading uses plain HTTP requests, so the model is only called for writing and reply handling.
A dashboard shows an outbox of drafted replies, with conversations handed back to a human.
Built for owners who want outbound without a per-token bill.
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: The clever part is moving everything that does not need a model out of the model loop, which is why the running cost is near zero. Experiment: point Harvey at a list of 50 local prospects for a side project and measure replies per hundred emails against your last manual push.

top_picks.title: argonne-lcf/ChemGraph
top_picks.summary: ChemGraph is an agent framework that connects natural-language requests to molecule building, simulation and reporting, using LangGraph, ASE, RDKit and MCP, with MACE and TBLite calculators and distributed runs on ALCF systems. A Deep Agent evaluation harness merged on Oct 22 after about a dozen commits that week.
top_picks.results: 12 commits in the window; latest release v0.7.0 (Sep 11); Oct 22 merge of pull request 256 adds Deep Agent evaluation with checkpointed, preflighted runs. Maintained by a national-lab team; 167 stars. Science bonus +0.5 included in score.
key_takeaways: Runs from the command line, Python, a Streamlit app or as an MCP server.
Local workflows use ASE calculators such as EMT and MACE; optional docking, XANES and retrieval add-ons.
This week's work is about scoring agents on chemistry tasks, not adding features.
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: The clever part is shipping an evaluation harness beside the chemistry agent, so a skeptical scientist can see pass rates before trusting it. Experiment: pick five calculations your researchers run by hand each week and let ChemGraph attempt them with MACE, then have a scientist grade the outputs.

items.title: thesysdev/openui

items.title: makecindy/cindy
items.summary: Cindy is an open-source desktop agent that combines several harnesses, models and tools and works on your real local files. It added 1,514 stars this week and ships a release every couple of days (v0.1.115 on Oct 23).

sections.title: Show HN and Indie Builds
sections.description: Show HN posts with a repo or live write-up, plus indie and hobby builds.

items.title: dsmurrell/onkey
items.summary: OnKey is a free Mac singing trainer that listens to the song playing in Spotify, Apple Music or YouTube, learns the singer's melody from one play and draws your pitch over it. The builder wrote the first version by asking Claude Code to detect both pitches.
items.results: Show HN: 233 points, 91 comments; repo created Oct 18, 308 stars, v0.1.0 on Oct 22; requires Apple Silicon and macOS 14.2 or later.

items.title: qwen3-4b-deslop
items.summary: A solo builder fine-tuned Qwen3-4B on an M2 MacBook Air so it writes without em dashes, 'not X, but Y' or lists of three, and the slop score fell from 121 to 12.5 per 1,000 words on 40 held-out prompts.
items.results: Show HN: 158 points, 113 comments. Author reports 288 teacher prompts, 161 selected answers, rank-16 LoRA, one to three hours per round, 30 of 30 factual questions correct. Self-reported results from one sample per prompt.
items.author: Erik Markus Kannike

items.title: AbdullahAlhariri/penmentor
items.summary: penmentor marks up handwritten maths in xournal++ with one key: Claude, Gemini or GPT circles the slip like a teacher, gives hints instead of answers and builds a manim animation of the idea. It runs on the user's own model subscription.
items.results: Show HN: 66 points, 9 comments; 131 stars; created Oct 17.

items.title: anubhavmalhotra/r2d2-tv
items.summary: R2D2 gives a webOS TV a local home screen, a private remote browser and a push-to-talk voice assistant, with a Linux host running Chromium and the voice models. The README warns the TV components run as root on one firmware build.
items.results: Show HN: 109 points, 79 comments; 63 stars; created Oct 21; 5 commits through Oct 24.
items.recurrence_note: Same pattern as last week's tv-vibehack: reclaiming a vendor TV, here with a voice assistant.

items.title: jamro/tiny-engineer
items.summary: Tiny Engineer is a desk robot that moves, changes its face and rings a bell as your coding agent reads files, writes code and finishes tasks, wired through Cursor and Claude Code hooks or a simple HTTP call. It added 176 stars this week on the C++ trending page.
items.results: 176 weekly stars (GitHub Trending, C++, Oct 25); 892 total; 12 commits in the window; v0.2.0 on Oct 5; the maker is polling interest in a $15 to $20 assembled board.

items.summary: McD Money Saver is a skill built on McDonald's MCP access that sorts coupons, points and bundles to work out the cheapest way to order. It was an entry in a McDonald's developer-day contest and has 347 stars after two days.
items.results: 347 stars since creation on Oct 22; README is in Chinese and says it was built with Tencent WorkBuddy for a contest.

items.title: amosblomqvist/learnharness

items.results: 1,679 stars nine days after creation (weekly delta not isolated); at least 50 commits in the window; AGPL-3.0.

items.title: omnara-ai/omnara
items.summary: Omnara is an open-source API for durable agents: one call creates an agent, with sandboxes, secrets, permissions and state stored in Postgres so idle agents cost nothing. It is pitched as a self-hostable alternative to managed-agent services.
items.results: Show HN: 114 points, 34 comments; 3,258 total stars; 26 commits in the window; omnarad v0.2.11 on Oct 24.

items.title: Asymptote-Labs/agent-beacon

items.results: 972 weekly stars (GitHub Trending, Go, Oct 25); 2,808 total; at least 100 commits in the window.

sections.title: Automation Wins
sections.description: Automations and pipelines with numbers attached, from GitHub and Hacker News. n8n and Make community pages had no dated, numbers-backed workflow inside the window.

items.title: C4rohan/Lampline
items.summary: Lampline is an open-source, self-hosted voice-agent platform that imports agents from Google's Dialogflow CX and tests them with real phone calls graded against checks. The README puts running cost at about $0.02 to $0.17 a call versus $0.50.
items.results: README states about $0.02 to $0.17 per call versus $0.50 (builder-reported, not independently tested); 267 stars since creation Oct 19; 97 commits; v0.4.0 on Oct 22.

items.title: this+that: an AI-written wiki of 45,047 Enron emails
items.summary: A small team had an AI read 45,047 Enron emails and write 214 pages holding 49,401 facts, each quoting the sentence in the email it came from. A second AI audit found 93% of sampled facts fully supported and none of 500 wrong at the core.
items.results: Show HN: 70 points, 56 comments. Reported: 57 proposed types, 54 kept; facts dropped unless the sentence matches the email word for word; audit by a second AI (self-reported).

items.title: mastra-ai/mastra @mastra/core 1.79.0

items.title: ollama/ollama v0.40.11
items.summary: Ollama v0.40.11 lets `ollama run` speak a reply aloud on macOS and serves audio through an OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech endpoint, and adds the d3 decision-model family in 2B to 27B sizes.
items.results: Release published Oct 24; speech is macOS-only in this release.

items.results: Release published Oct 23.

sections.title: Emerging Patterns
sections.description: Patterns visible across this week's repos.

items.title: Owners are reclaiming vendor TV screens with a coding agent
items.summary: A second wave of TV launchers followed last week's tv-vibehack: aerial-tv (5,021 stars), free-my-tv (4,616) and r2d2-tv (63 stars, 109 HN points). Each installs through an AI assistant over the local network and keeps an undo path.
items.recurrence_note: Extends last week's tv-vibehack pattern with three new implementations.
key_takeaways: Two of the three were created within the week and passed 4,000 stars in days.
Setup is delegated to Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity with a prompt in the README.

items.title: Science groups are shipping agents with evaluation and citations
items.summary: Three science repos pair an agent with proof: ChemGraph merged an evaluation harness, idfkit-mcp wraps EnergyPlus in 37 validated tools, and the computational-chemistry skill library cites a J. Chem. Theory Comput. paper.
key_takeaways: Validation layers and evaluation harnesses ship in the same repo as the agent.
MCP and skills are the common packaging for simulators.

items.title: Agent memory is becoming vendor-neutral
items.summary: ai-memory (3,254 weekly stars) and agent-beacon (972) both give one memory to many coding agents so a task can move between tools without re-explaining, and Omnara stores durable agent state in Postgres.
key_takeaways: Handoffs are becoming typed protocols rather than chat summaries.
Both repos support 20 or more harnesses or the major CLIs.
